title: refactor(sdk): return raw model registry data
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Returns `/models` entries unchanged, preserving server order, snake-case names, and fields added after an SDK release.
- Removes the parallel `ModelCatalogItem` DTO, field defaults/renames, SDK category sorting, and display-ready pricing labels.
- Moves model ID fallback, known-category ordering, pricing labels, and selector sorting into the React/playground/UI consumers that display them.
- Retains the authenticated allow-set needed by the current app access UI. Net change: 226 fewer lines.

Checks:
- SDK: 30 tests, typecheck, and build
- UI: 6 tests, typecheck, and build
- React modules and playground: typecheck and Vite builds
- Biome and `git diff --check`
- Live `/models`: 227 raw entries; first entry retained all 15 server fields

gist.headline: The catalog stopped gardening
gist.blurb: The SDK now hands model registry entries over exactly as the server grew them. No surprise pruning, relabeling, or alphabetizing by a helpful little middle layer.
gist.summary: The SDK now returns raw `/models` registry entries in server order, preserving snake_case names and all fields—including fields added after an SDK release—while React, playground, and UI consumers handle display sorting and pricing labels locally.
gist.impact: Developers can use the full live model metadata from the 227-entry registry without waiting for an SDK DTO update, while model pickers retain their familiar curated ordering and labels.
gist.visual_concept: Depict the model registry as a flourishing garden of labeled seed packets and data flowers, each kept in its original arrangement rather than being rearranged into decorative rows. Polli, wearing tiny librarian glasses, gently passes an unedited catalog scroll from a retro terminal to a helpful CRT robot, while the display shelf nearby neatly sorts only the flowers meant for visitors.
